message.content:
Yes—Atlanta residents can file a noise‑complaint with the city’s authorities.  
Here’s how you can do it:

| Method | Contact Info | How to Use |
|--------|--------------|------------|
| **Online Form** | [Noise Complaint – City of Atlanta](https://www.atlantaga.gov/government/departments/department-of-public-safety/police-department/code-enforcement/noise-complaint) | Fill out the web form with details (date, time, location, description, and your contact info). Submit and you’ll receive a confirmation email. |
| **Phone (Non‑Emergency)** | 404‑656‑4000 | Call the Atlanta Police Department’s non‑emergency line and ask to speak with the Code Enforcement unit. They’ll take your complaint over the phone. |
| **Email** | noise@atlantaga.gov | Send an email describing the incident, including time, location, and any evidence (photos, videos, or recordings). |
| **In‑Person** | 101 Marietta Street NE, Atlanta, GA 30303 | Visit the City Hall or the Police Department’s Code Enforcement office during business hours. Bring any documentation you have. |

### Quick Reference

- **City Code**: Noise ordinances are codified in the Atlanta Municipal Code (Title 12, Chapter 12.1). They prohibit “loud, continuous, or disruptive” sounds after 10 p.m. on weekdays and 11 p.m. on weekends, among other restrictions.  
- **Response Time**: The city typically responds within 24–48 hours, but urgent cases can be escalated to the police.  
- **Follow‑Up**: If you don’t hear back within a week, call the non‑emergency line again or check the status of your online submission.

Feel free to use whichever method is most convenient for you. If you’re dealing with a recurring issue, keep a log of dates, times, and any actions taken; this helps the city track patterns and enforce the ordinance more effectively.
